title: Choose the homepage composition
question: Three page architectures for the homepage and the service/product detail templates. The visual world stays exactly as pinned: achromatic paper, one peach/sienna pair, serif display never bold, no icons, no card shadows. What changes is the skeleton. Lock one.

options.label: The Ledger
options.thesis: The homepage is one continuous ruled register: every claim is an entry, and its evidence is cited in the margin beside it.
options.viewport: A three-column register: running index at left, the claim and a peach action row in the main column, cited figures and client wordmarks in the right margin, and the first service entries already begun below the fold line.
options.risk: A register can read as dry paperwork; it only works if the type is confident enough to carry a whole viewport with no image at all.

raised.raise: Every claim now carries a printed reference mark, the way a boarding pass segments a journey into labelled parts.
Entries accumulate: each one keeps the cross-references of the ones before it, so the register reads as a record rather than a list.

options.label: The Proof Spine
options.thesis: A permanent evidence column holds the twelve client marks, the three figures and the founder, while the right column argues beside it.
options.viewport: Asymmetric split: a peach-headed evidence register pinned at the left holding the figures, twelve client wordmarks and the founder, with the claim, the action and a compressed seven-line service list at the right.
options.risk: The pinned rail is a familiar pattern, so the citation system has to do real work or this is a sidebar with a footnote drawn on it.

options.label: The Chronology
options.thesis: The page is the studio's record read from 2013 to now along a single rule, with the current chapter carrying the colour.
materials: a peach band for the live chapter
options.viewport: A rule at 300px with era labels in the left margin, a peach band carrying the claim and the action as the current chapter, and the first era entry opening below it.
options.risk: The record has only one real date, 2013; era labels keep it honest, but inventing dates for clients or products would break the studio's truth rule.

options.label: Segmented Pass
options.lineage: a boarding pass beside a gate board
options.thesis: The page becomes a segmented document: scope, deliverables, ownership and warranty as labelled stubs, with a live board reranking what is current.
options.viewport: A pass-shaped document split into labelled stubs, with the primary action on the tear-off edge.
options.risk: A boarding pass means travel, not procurement; it holds product clarity but not audience identification.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and beats the grounded list on clarity, but a travel artifact identifies the buyer poorly. Its reference-mark discipline was donated to the Ledger.
options.kept: Labelled segmentation and a printed reference mark per claim.

options.label: Fold Sequence
options.lineage: one uncut sheet folded into a crane
options.thesis: One continuous sheet that passes through thirty-two numbered states, each carrying every earlier crease.
options.viewport: A single sheet with a numbered fold margin and the active state marked.
options.risk: Its vermilion ground and diagrammatic subject would replace the pinned palette, and a fold diagram is a picture of a craft, not a studio page.
options.case: Declined on identity: the world is a paper crane, not this studio. Loses on audience identification and on product clarity both.
options.kept: Accumulated state: entries that keep the marks of the ones before them.

options.label: Title Sequence
options.thesis: The page is a timed sequence of full-bleed cards, one idea per card, in hard asymmetry.
options.viewport: One full-bleed field carrying a single cut shape and one line of type.
options.risk: Cut-paper silhouettes are invented imagery, which this studio's own rules forbid, and a timed sequence makes a buyer wait for the facts.
options.case: Declined on truth and clarity: the shapes would have to be authored from nothing, and the sequence hides the offer behind timing.
options.kept: One dominant move per section instead of a balanced two-column.

options.label: Step Row
options.lineage: an early-80s rhythm machine step row
options.thesis: The whole page hangs off one unbroken horizontal line that never wraps, only scales.
options.viewport: A sixteen-step row as the page's single unbroken line under a readout.
options.risk: Candy-coloured keys on charcoal would replace the pinned palette outright, and a step sequencer is a costume of a tool.
options.case: Declined on identity: the palette is the opposite of the pinned achromatic paper, and the sequencer means nothing to a buyer.
options.kept: One continuous element that holds the page together across its whole length.

options.label: Gravity Rain
options.lineage: a rain garden with local gravity
options.thesis: Each region obeys a visible local rule, stated once and then never broken.
options.viewport: A garden field with rain bending toward each object and one level legend.
options.risk: A dream world identifies nobody in this audience, and bending baselines would break the reading of a five-locale site.
options.case: Declined on identification: no business buyer sees their own decision in a gravity garden.
options.kept: A rule system stated once in the margin and obeyed by every entry after it.

options.label: Nightboard
options.lineage: a dial-up bulletin board at 2 a.m.
options.thesis: The page is one character grid, and every element is a cell in it.
options.viewport: An 80 by 25 character grid with a centred title screen.
options.risk: Terminal cyan and magenta would replace the pinned palette, and a monospace costume is exactly what the studio's serif restraint refuses.
options.case: Declined on identity: the palette and the monospace costume both contradict the pinned world.
options.kept: A strict column measure that nothing is allowed to exceed.
